prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability/entitlement to compensation is conceded; this is a pure valuation trial where claimant should recover for both the direct taking of the 9.5-acre strip and some reduced-access severance damage to the western parcel, but the collateral estoppel ruling forecloses a 'total loss' theory and claimant's prior reversal for insufficient proof creates real evidentiary risk. The direct-take component likely lands in the $400K-$1.3M range depending on the strip's zoning classification; the severance-damages component is almost certainly larger but cannot be quantified from this record because no post-taking valuation figure is provided.

outcome.description: After a four-day January 2018 trial the Court of Claims credited the State's appraiser (with its own adjustments, preappropriation value $52,339 per acre or $1,662,810), found the western remainder's post-taking highest and best use was multifamily residential, and awarded KKS $744,500 in direct and consequential damages. The Third Department affirmed the amended judgment on October 29, 2020. (An earlier award of $532,000 had been reversed in 2014.)
